1.explanation:
• unminified-javascript-test.js: contains the core test logic and fixture patterns used to detect unminified JS and calculate savings; key to understanding why whitespace in comments triggers a failure.
• unminified-css-test.js: parallels the JS audit’s approach for CSS, illustrating how similar whitespace/comment handling is implemented and tested.
• byte-efficiency-audit-test.js: provides the shared test harness for byte-efficiency audits, showing common setup and expectation patterns.
• audit-test.js: the generic audit testing framework, demonstrating how artifacts are faked and audits are invoked in tests.
• test-utils.js: offers helper functions to generate fake network records and artifacts; used across audit tests to simulate resource content and sizes.
• runner-test.js: shows how Lighthouse initializes and runs audits end-to-end in a simulated environment, useful for reproducing the full audit flow against a test page.
1.bug_scenario: In the Lighthouse “Opportunities” panel, the AMP component file “/v0/amp-date-picker-0.1.js” is flagged as not minified with ~139 KB savings, even though it’s served already minified. The root cause is a hard-coded copyright comment block that contains carriage returns and extra whitespace. This breaks Esprima’s minification check, causing the unminified-JavaScript audit to overestimate savings.
